name: Daniel Heinz
role: Head of the Digital Service Design & Innovation Lab
agenda: I study how organizations change when data and AI enter everyday work: which responsibilities shift, which capabilities people need, and how existing systems can support renewal.
approach: My work combines qualitative field research with design science. Working systems let us study organizational change while it happens.

appointments.title: Head of the Digital Service Design & Innovation Lab

education.title: Dr. rer. pol. in Information Systems
education.note: Dissertation: Smart Service Innovation in Incumbent Firms. Summa cum laude.

visits: Visiting research stays at the University of Cambridge (2024) and The University of Queensland (2022).
advising: I provide day-to-day doctoral advising and supervise bachelor’s and master’s theses.
funding: I lead proposal development and scientific work in publicly funded projects and industry collaborations at KIT. These collaborations provide settings in which to study digital services and organizational change in practice.
service: Head of the Conferences Division, Die WI e.V.
Chair for Workshops, Tutorials & Community Events, WI 2027
outsideWork: Outside work I volunteer with DPSG, Germany’s largest scout association. I lead its program for 15- to 21-year-olds in the Freiburg diocese, train youth leaders, and from 2023 to 2025 led CrOver, an international camp for about 250 scouts funded by Erasmus+.
